text: WEYBURN, Feb. 9, 1916. The worst blizzard of the winter has been raging over this district since Monday night, and at the time of writing there is no sign of a let-up. A gale from the northwest is driving the snow so thick that a man cannot see the length of his team, and the thermometer stood at 34 below this morning. No trains have reached the city from either direction for two days, the drifts in the cuts east of town being reported higher than the cars. Several farmers who came in for supplies on Monday are stormbound at the hotels. Fears are held for a young homesteader named Pettersen, who set out for his claim north of town on Monday afternoon and has not been heard from.
label: winter

text: Ice accretion of 15 to 25 mm from freezing rain along the Truro to Antigonish corridor, 12 February 2008. About 45,000 customers without power at the peak.
label: winter

text: For nine straight nights in early February 1962 the temperature in Edmonton fell below forty below. Hospitals treated dozens of people for frostbite, most of them men who had walked home from stalled cars. Water mains froze under several residential streets, and the city ran tank trucks to the worst-hit blocks. Garages could not keep up with calls for dead batteries.
label: winter

text: Freezing rain fell almost without pause for thirty hours across Sarnia-Lambton on 9 and 10 February 2001, building up as much as 30 mm of clear ice on trees, wires and roads. By the second morning the cracking of branches sounded like gunfire in the older neighbourhoods. Hydro poles snapped along the concession roads, leaving some 50,000 customers in the dark, many of them for four or five days in sub-zero temperatures. Dairy farmers without generators milked by hand or dumped milk they could not cool. Warming centres opened in Petrolia and Forest, and the county asked neighbouring utilities for line crews. Two people died of carbon monoxide poisoning from generators run indoors.
label: winter

text: Drifts twelve feet deep stalled two passenger trains near Bathurst, N.B., in January 1905; the passengers were fed by nearby farmers for thirty hours until a snowplough got through.
label: winter

text: Re: death by exposure of Louis Cardinal, trapper. On the 3rd instant I received word at Lac La Biche that Cardinal had not returned to his cabin since before Christmas. With a guide and two dog teams I followed his line northward and on the 5th found his body some four miles from the cabin, lying in the lee of a spruce thicket. It is evident he was caught by the blizzard of 27 December and lost his way in the drifting snow; his dogs had broken their traces and two were found frozen near by. There are no marks of violence. The body was brought in by toboggan and handed over to his relatives for burial. (Constable's report, R.N.W.M.P., January 1913)
label: winter

text: Highway 1 is closed between Swift Current and Gull Lake due to zero visibility in blowing snow and drifting across the driving lanes. Motorists are advised not to travel. (Highway hotline, 6 December 2016, 07:15)
label: winter

text: Snowbound. Diary of a farm wife near Russell, Man., March 1920. Third day of the storm. Cannot see the barn from the kitchen window. Will tied a rope from the porch to the stable door to find his way out to the stock. Coal nearly gone; burning fence posts. The children have not been to school since Monday.
label: winter

text: A slow-moving winter storm dumped between 40 and 60 cm of snow on the Annapolis Valley and the South Shore on 28 and 29 January 1987, with winds gusting to 90 km/h piling drifts two metres high. Highway 101 was closed for most of a day after dozens of cars and transport trucks became stuck. Snowplough operators worked 20-hour shifts, and the RCMP used snowmobiles to reach motorists stranded overnight. Schools stayed closed for three days. At least two men died of heart attacks while shovelling.
label: winter

text: Cold snap, Yellowknife, January 1975: a week of temperatures between -45 and -50 C. Vehicles would not start, the school bus service was suspended, and the mine ran its surface crews in short shifts to limit frostbite.
label: winter

text: OTTAWA, Dec. 14, 1910. The first real snowstorm of the season descended on the capital yesterday with a vengeance. Fifteen inches of snow fell in eighteen hours, and a stiff east wind banked it against doors and fences until many householders had to dig their way out this morning. The street railway was tied up for most of the day, and the sweepers worked through the night to clear the main lines. Delivery wagons gave up early, and the sleighs came out in force.
label: winter

text: Sleet and freezing rain glazed every street in Hamilton on the morning of 19 March 1958, and by noon the hospital emergency room had treated more than 120 people for broken wrists, ankles and hips. Buses were taken off the Mountain routes after several slid backward down the escarpment access roads.
label: winter

text: The weather office at Churchill recorded a wind chill equivalent of nearly -60 on the morning of 22 January 1966. Outdoor work at the port was halted. A northwest wind of 50 km/h had been blowing off the bay for two days with the air temperature near -40, and exposed skin froze in under a minute. Schoolchildren were kept home, and the hospital treated several men for frostbitten cheeks and fingers.
label: winter

text: Two snowmobilers travelling between Arviat and Whale Cove were caught in a whiteout on 11 February 2009 and spent two nights in a snow shelter they dug beside their machines. Winds of 70 km/h and temperatures near -38 C kept search teams in the hamlet until the storm eased. Both men were found alive, with frostbite to their hands and faces, and were flown to Winnipeg for treatment.
label: winter

text: A heavy snowfall on the night of 3 March 1934 brought Halifax to a standstill: 22 inches by morning, the street railway dead, and the dockyard closed. Men were hired at thirty cents an hour to shovel the tracks.
label: winter

text: Freezing rain overnight, 21-22 November 1995, Fredericton region. Ice build-up of 10 to 15 mm brought down trees and wires; NB Power reported 38,000 customers without service at 6 a.m. Schools closed. Numerous minor collisions on untreated roads.
label: winter

text: Report of the stock association, Maple Creek district, spring 1911. The deep snow of the winter, followed in February by a thaw and a hard freeze that left a crust of ice over the range, made it impossible for cattle to rustle grass. Herds that wintered out without hay lost from a quarter to a third of their numbers, and the coulees are full of carcasses. Several of the smaller ranchers are ruined.
label: winter

text: KITCHENER, Feb. 3, 1956. A storm that dropped more than a foot of snow on the Twin Cities overnight has closed every rural school in Waterloo County and left side roads impassable. Milk trucks could not reach the dairies until noon, and the city called in private trucks to help its ploughs clear King Street.
label: winter

text: Extreme cold warning in effect for Prince Albert. Wind chill values of -45 to -50 expected overnight. Frostbite can develop within minutes on exposed skin. (Weather office bulletin, 13 January 2004)
label: winter

text: For farm families in the Interlake, the winter of 1955 is remembered for the March blizzard that sealed them in for more than a week. The storm blew for three days without a break, and when it ended the drifts were so high that some families had to tunnel out through the snow to reach their barns. Municipal bulldozers made little headway on the side roads. When word came that a child near Fisher Branch was seriously ill, a ski-equipped plane landed on a frozen field and flew her to hospital in Winnipeg. Air force planes dropped bundles of bread, flour and medicine to isolated homesteads, and several farmers lost cattle that could not be fed or watered in time.
label: winter

text: Sleet storm at London, Ont., February 1909: telegraph and telephone wires down in every direction, and many fine shade trees broken by the weight of the ice.
label: winter

text: A night of freezing rain on 23 January 2011 left Prince Edward Island glazed under 10 to 20 mm of ice. Maritime Electric reported 30,000 customers without power by morning, mostly in Kings County, where downed lines blocked several rural roads. Schools were closed island-wide and the Confederation Bridge restricted high-sided vehicles.
label: winter

text: Climate summary: the blizzard of 22 to 24 March 1991 in southern Manitoba. Winds of 70 to 90 km/h combined with 25 to 35 cm of fresh snow to cut visibility to near zero for 36 hours. The Trans-Canada Highway was closed from Winnipeg to the Ontario border and from Portage la Prairie to Brandon. About 300 stranded motorists were taken in by farm families, community halls and a Hutterite colony near Elie. The storm struck at the height of calving season, and ranchers in the southwest reported heavy losses of newborn calves. Hydro crews dealt with more than 200 broken poles where drifted snow and wind brought lines down.
label: winter

text: Snow, Nanaimo, 27 and 28 December 1964: 45 cm on the ground. City buses off the road; hospital staff brought in by Jeep. The snow was wet and heavy, and its weight brought down branches and wires in the older parts of town. With few ploughs and fewer tire chains, the city all but stopped for three days, and the ferries ran nearly empty.
label: winter

text: Harrington Harbour, 14 February 1925. Dear Mother, we have had three weeks of the hardest cold anyone here can remember, never above twenty below and often thirty-five, with a wind off the ice that cuts through every coat. The harbour is frozen solid out to the islands. I have had nine cases of frostbite in a fortnight; one young sealer, caught out on the ice when the weather closed in, has lost three toes. We keep the stove going night and day and still the water pail freezes by morning.
label: winter

text: Storm day. All schools in the Eastern School District are closed today, 15 February 2010, following 30 cm of snow and strong winds overnight. Buses will not run.
label: winter

text: Post journal, Norway House, January 1902. 14th. Wind N.W., very cold, 48 below by the thermometer at sunrise. Men could not haul wood. 15th. Same, drifting badly. Ink frozen in the bottle. 16th. Calmer, 44 below. Two families came in from the lake, their nets frozen in and no fish taken for a week; gave them flour and pemmican on account. 17th. Snowing heavily all day.
label: winter

text: A week of temperatures between -40 and -45 C in mid-January 2005 kept Grande Prairie's tow trucks booked around the clock. The city opened its recreation centre as a warming station after a furnace failure at an apartment block left 60 residents without heat. Doctors at the regional hospital treated several homeless men for frostbite.
label: winter

text: Freezing drizzle, Gander airport, 8 December 1976: runway closed for nine hours while crews sanded and scraped ice.
label: winter

text: SAINT JOHN, Feb. 22, 1960. The storm that buried the city under twenty inches of snow on Friday was followed by a night of rain and then a sharp freeze, leaving streets sheathed in ice and drifts as hard as concrete. Sidewalks were impassable, and the hospital set up extra beds for people hurt in falls. The weight of wet snow and ice brought down part of the roof of a curling rink in the north end; no one was inside. City crews will need most of the week to open the side streets.
label: winter

text: A thin layer of freezing drizzle under fresh snow turned Edmonton's roads into a skating rink on the morning of 9 November 2010. Police reported more than 300 minor collisions before noon, transit buses ran up to an hour late, and the city sent every sander it had onto the arterial roads.
label: winter

text: Cold wave, Winnipeg, February 1929: 47 below at the Agricultural College on the 2nd. Plumbers are in great demand and coal dealers cannot keep up with orders.
label: winter

text: Blizzard conditions persisted in Cambridge Bay for nearly 72 hours, from 18 to 21 February 1995. Winds gusting over 100 km/h drove snow so hard that some houses were buried to the eaves and residents had to climb out through windows. The airport was closed and fuel deliveries stopped. Hamlet staff and Rangers checked on elders by snow machine whenever the visibility allowed, using rope lines between buildings. A young man who tried to walk home from a friend's house during the second night was found the next morning curled up in the lee of a fuel tank, badly frostbitten but alive.
label: winter

text: CHARLOTTETOWN, March 9, 1921. The Island is cut off from the mainland once more, the ice boats being unable to cross on account of the heavy snow and the driving northeast wind. Drifts on Queen Street are higher than a man's head. Country people have not been able to bring in produce for four days.
label: winter

text: Glaze storm, Ottawa, 28 December 1942: trees and wires down in Sandy Hill and the Glebe, streetcars stalled by iced trolley wires. Wartime shortages of men and materials slowed the repairs, and some houses were without electric light into the New Year. The Experimental Farm reported serious damage to its shelterbelts.
label: winter

text: A late-season blizzard swept across southern Alberta from 9 to 11 April 2010, dumping up to 50 cm of snow driven by winds of 80 km/h. It caught ranchers in the middle of calving. Many worked through the nights, carrying newborn calves into barns and kitchens to warm them, but losses were still heavy where cattle drifted with the storm into fences and coulees. The Trans-Canada Highway was closed between Medicine Hat and the Saskatchewan border, and RCMP escorted stranded truckers to a community hall in Irvine. Power was out for two days in parts of Cypress County.
label: winter

text: The Townships, January 1952. Snow-blocked roads kept the farms north of Stanstead isolated for most of a week after a storm that left drifts eight feet deep along the line fences. Milk was hauled out by horse and sleigh to meet the plough at the main road, as in the old days.
label: winter

text: Snowfall warning ended. Storm totals: 52 cm at Kenora airport, 4 and 5 December 2013.
label: winter

text: TORONTO, Jan. 15, 1912. The bitter cold that has gripped the city for five days claimed two more lives yesterday. A labourer was found frozen to death in a lane off Queen Street, and an elderly woman living alone in the Ward was discovered dead in her room, the stove cold. The House of Industry lodged more than 300 men last night, and the coal dealers report that they cannot fill orders from poorer districts fast enough. The mercury touched 18 below at the observatory.
label: winter

text: Saskatoon's two hospitals treated 34 cases of frostbite in ten days during the cold snap of late December 1996, several requiring amputation of fingers or toes. Most of the patients had been caught outdoors without proper clothing after leaving disabled vehicles.
label: winter
